name: config-versioning
title: Configuration versioning: save, publish, history, apply
description: Every save of a scenario's prompt and first message is a version, with an optional note. On a live scenario a save waits for a publish; history compares any two versions, applies an older one or copies it to edit, and a call's details show the version it ran on.

"use client"

import { HugeiconsIcon, type IconSvgElement } from "@hugeicons/react"

/**
 * Wraps a HugeIcons glyph into the call shape the rest of the repo uses —
 * `<CloseIcon />` — so the shadcn primitives keep sizing it through their own
 * `[&_svg]:size-4` rules and nothing needs a size prop.
 *
 * Every mockup keeps its icons in its own `icons.tsx` built from this. Import
 * the glyph once, name it for what it does in that screen, and the screen reads
 * in verbs rather than in icon-set trivia.
 */
export function icon(glyph: IconSvgElement, displayName: string) {
  const Icon = (
    props: Omit<React.ComponentProps<typeof HugeiconsIcon>, "icon">,
  ) => <HugeiconsIcon icon={glyph} strokeWidth={1.8} {...props} />
  Icon.displayName = displayName
  return Icon
}

import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
import { Label } from "@/components/ui/label"

/**
 * A scenario's Live switch, in the editor's header: one click, asks nothing
 * (TDD 3.1). DES-203 introduces it and DES-202 keeps it, so both import this
 * one. It was a button opening a popover with the switch inside — two clicks
 * for one value (feedback, 22 Oct 2026). What the popover said moves out:
 *
 *  - Who turned it on or off is the switch's tooltip. Toggling makes no
 *    version, so this is the only record of it.
 *  - What live means for saves is the toast that follows a toggle, said
 *    once at the moment it changes rather than on every visit.
 *
 * The switch sits in an outline control the height of the buttons beside
 * it, so the row reads as one set of controls. The whole control is the
 * label: a click anywhere on it flips the switch.
 */
export function LiveSwitch({
  live,
  canToggle,
  onToggle,
  toggled,
  pending = false,
}: {
  live: boolean
  /** Turning live on or off is its own permission, separate from editing. */
  canToggle: boolean
  onToggle: (on: boolean) => void
  /** Who last turned it on or off, and when. */
  toggled: { by: string; at: string } | null
  /** The change is on its way to the server. */
  pending?: boolean
}) {
  const hint = !canToggle
    ? "You don't have permission to turn this on or off."
    : toggled
      ? `Turned ${live ? "on" : "off"} by ${toggled.by === "You" ? "you" : toggled.by}, ${toggled.at}`
      : null

  const control = (
    <Button
      asChild
      className={canToggle ? "cursor-pointer" : "cursor-not-allowed"}
      variant="outline"
    >
      <Label htmlFor="live-switch">
        {pending ? <Spinner /> : null}
        Live
        <Switch
          checked={live}
          disabled={!canToggle || pending}
          id="live-switch"
          onCheckedChange={onToggle}
          size="sm"
        />
      </Label>
    </Button>
  )

  if (!hint) return control

  return (
    <Tooltip>
      <TooltipTrigger asChild>{control}</TooltipTrigger>
      <TooltipContent>{hint}</TooltipContent>
    </Tooltip>
  )
}

/**
 * Mock data for DES-202, configuration versioning. The model is the TDD,
 * "Live scenarios and configuration versioning" (Fatma Moanes, 22 Oct 2026):
 *
 *  - Scenarios only. The global prompt gets versions in a later release.
 *  - A version is the prompt and the first message, saved together and
 *    always restored together. Every save makes one, with an optional note,
 *    and records the version it was edited from. Versions are never edited
 *    or deleted.
 *  - Every scenario has a version in use: what the next call runs. On a live
 *    scenario a save does not move it; publishing does. On a scenario that
 *    is not live a save moves it straight away. Applying an older version
 *    points back at it and makes no new version.
 *  - Live is a switch and a badge. Turning it on or off changes nothing
 *    about which version runs.
 */

export type Field = { id: string; label: string; multiline: boolean }

export type Version = {
  n: number
  author: string
  /** Saved by the person looking. */
  mine: boolean
  at: string
  editedFrom: number | null
  /** The optional note left on save. */
  note: string | null
  body: Record<string, string>
}

/** One time a version was put in use: by a save on a scenario that is not
    live, by publishing, or by applying an older one. */
export type InUseEntry = {
  n: number
  by: string
  at: string
  how: "saved" | "published" | "applied"
}

export type Subject = {
  name: string
  fields: Field[]
  /** Newest first. */
  versions: Version[]
  /** The switch and the badge. Moving it changes no version. */
  live: boolean
  /** The version in use: what the next call runs. */
  inUse: number
  /** Every time a version was put in use, newest first, so the first is
      the version in use now. History reads it to say who applied each
      version and when (TDD 3.2). */
  log: InUseEntry[]
  /** Who last turned live on or off, and when. Toggling makes no version,
      so this is where the record of it shows. */
  toggled: { by: string; at: string } | null
}

/** What a reviewer can force, so every state the TDD names is reachable. */
export type CaseId =
  | "normal"
  | "conflict"

  | "history-fails"
  | "view-only"
  | "no-live-permission"
  | "publish-fails"
  | "apply-blocked"
  | "apply-skips"
